svg.title: From Protected Claim to Baseball-Style IDR
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-nsa-dispute-entry-path; chapter number: 1; title: From Protected Claim to Baseball-Style IDR; subtitle: Five operator moves that carry a surprise-billing dispute into arbitration; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Bill the plan directly; value: Step 1; detail: Billing the plan directly reveals whether No Surprises Act protections apply to the claim.; step: 02; label: Load every deadline into a tracker; value: Step 2; detail: Open-negotiation, initiation, and offer deadlines go into a tracker before the first dispute, because missing one by a day or two can invalidate the IDR.; step: 03; label: Run the 30-business-day open negotiation; value: Step 3; detail: Payment flows through a 30-business-day open negotiation before baseball-style IDR anchored to the QPA, the 2019 median contracted rate indexed for inflation.; step: 04; label: Pull 4 years of prior in-network rates; value: Step 4; detail: Prior in-network rates from the past 4 years serve as a defense in IDR, alongside challenges to payer down-coding.; step: 05; label: Price the final offer for winner-takes-all; value: Step 5; detail: The arbitrator picks one offer and not the average; in one Arizona self-funded case a $42,000 anesthesia bill closed just over $21,000 against an $18,000 QPA.; caption: Protection check, deadline discipline, negotiation, evidence, and offer pricing form the entry path into federal IDR.; assumptions note: Step order reflects the sequence of operator gates and pro-tips as reported; dollar figures come from a single self-funded anesthesia case and are not presented as typical.; note: Attributed to CMSHHSgov (aQ87InetyaA), PYA, PC (j1DGgPw1__E), and Jentry Harris (LNSPlo2_U3c).

text.title: From Protected Claim to Baseball-Style IDR
text.tspan: From Protected Claim to Baseball-Style IDR

circle.title: step: 01; label: Bill the plan directly; value: Step 1; detail: Billing the plan directly reveals whether No Surprises Act protections apply to the claim.

text.title: Billing the plan directly reveals whether No Surprises Act protections apply to the claim.

circle.title: step: 02; label: Load every deadline into a tracker; value: Step 2; detail: Open-negotiation, initiation, and offer deadlines go into a tracker before the first dispute, because missing one by a day or two can invalidate the IDR.

text.title: Load every deadline into a tracker
Open-negotiation, initiation, and offer deadlines go into a tracker before the first dispute, because missing one by a day or two can invalidate the IDR.

circle.title: step: 03; label: Run the 30-business-day open negotiation; value: Step 3; detail: Payment flows through a 30-business-day open negotiation before baseball-style IDR anchored to the QPA, the 2019 median contracted rate indexed for inflation.

text.title: Payment flows through a 30-business-day open negotiation before baseball-style IDR anchored to the QPA, the 2019 median contracted rate indexed for inflation.

circle.title: step: 04; label: Pull 4 years of prior in-network rates; value: Step 4; detail: Prior in-network rates from the past 4 years serve as a defense in IDR, alongside challenges to payer down-coding.

text.title: Pull 4 years of prior in-network rates
Prior in-network rates from the past 4 years serve as a defense in IDR, alongside challenges to payer down-coding.

circle.title: step: 05; label: Price the final offer for winner-takes-all; value: Step 5; detail: The arbitrator picks one offer and not the average; in one Arizona self-funded case a $42,000 anesthesia bill closed just over $21,000 against an $18,000 QPA.

text.title: Price the final offer for winner-takes-all
The arbitrator picks one offer and not the average; in one Arizona self-funded case a $42,000 anesthesia bill closed just over $21,000 against an $18,000 QPA.
